% 04.06.2025  CRL.M.A. 17331/2025-EXEMP.
1. Exemption allowed subject to just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

This is an application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (B.N.S.S) seeking anticipatory bail on behalf of the applicant in FIR No. 180/2025 under Section 420/468/471 IPC, Police Station Rajouri Garden, Delhi.
4. Issue notice.
5. Notice is accepted by Mr. Bahri, learned APP and Mr. Kunal Sharma, This is a digitally signed order.

6. Status report, if any, be filed by the prosecution within a period of one week.
Complainant may also file a reply in a week.
7. Rejoinder/ response to the status report and reply of the complainant be also filed by the petitioner within a period of two days thereafter.
8. It is not disputed that the present petitioner is the paternal uncle of husband of the complainant.
It is also not disputed that the petitioner was granted protection by the Sessions Court vide order dated 19th April 2025 till 22nd May 2025.

It is also submitted by Mr. Aggarwal, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner that the petitioner had joined the investigations on 19th April 2025 and 25th April 2025, wherein whatever material and information was available was tendered to the Investigating Officer.

9. Mr. Aggarwal, also submits that in response to the notice under Section 95 of the BNSS, 2023, a reply dated 25th April 2025 providing all relevant documents available was tendered by the petitioner, who also informed that the alleged transfer of shares including the Form SH-4 was not available with him and those documents would be available with the Register of Companies (RoC).

He also submits that the IO had, vide the status report dated 28th April, 2025, admitted that no Form SH-4 was available in the RoC.
10.
Thus, according to him, the question of any forgery having been committed does not arise.

That apart, learned counsel also submits that the allegation against the applicant appears to be stemming from the marital discord between the complainant and the husband of the complainant who happens to be the nephew of the applicant.
He thus submits that the dismissal or the rejection of the anticipatory bail applications by the This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/06/2025 at 12:07:03 judgment dated 22nd May 2025, overlooks the basic facts.

11. He also submits that in all probability, the application of the applicant before the learned Session Judge was dismissed on account of it being a common judgment in respect of all the co-accused persons, some of whom may be directly related to the complainants.

12. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent / Complainant submits that the applicant has not disclosed or produced the Form SH-4 and the minutes of the meeting vide which the alleged transfers were made, which itself shows that there has been a concealment of facts, and points towards forgery committed by the applicant along with other co-accused persons.

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel also vehemently submits that the complainant had clearly alleged that her signatures have been forged on Form SH-4 and also submits that the minutes of the meeting reflect that Form SH-4 was recorded and the transfer of 18,000 shares which originally stood in the name of the complainant, were illegally transferred in the name of the husband of the complainant.
14. He alleges that in the minutes of the meeting where the shares were transferred fraudulently, the petitioner too was present.

15. Having regard to the fact that petitioner was protected by the Sessions Court previously and that he had joined investigations and being of the prima facie opinion that dispute arises out of acrimonious marital relations between the complainant and the nephew of the petitioner, this Court is of the considered opinion that the till the time the replies are filed and the matter is heard, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant subject to the applicant joining the investigations and cooperating with the Investigating Officer.

The petitioner is directed not to leave the State of Delhi without taking permission of the Trial Court.
17. In addition to the above, at the request of learned APP, the petitioner is directed to present himself before the IO at 04.00 P.M. on 05th June 2025 at Police Station Rajouri Garden.
18. The aforesaid order is being passed keeping in view the situation obtaining in the present case.

19. List the matter for consideration on 13.06.2025 before the Vacation Bench.
